Primary request: one photorealistic ORIGINAL architectural interpretation of the nineteenth-century central hall dome of Palau Güell in Barcelona, as a plausible circa-1890s space, seen from the exact centre of the hall looking straight UP. Exactly 1536 x 1024 pixels, landscape 3:2, opaque RGB PNG; a round-looking centred dome subject fully composed within this shared landscape canvas, not a separate square crop.
Subject: a lofty dark warm-brown PARABOLIC dome resting on four parabolic arches, lined in rows of small crystalline hexagonal limestone pieces that decrease in size towards the central high ventilation aperture. Many small round perforations in individual stone pieces admit restrained points of genuine daylight, giving a starry-sky effect. The bright points are holes in masonry, not lamps or LEDs; slight daylight spill at their edges makes their physical depth apparent. The curved dark surface and height remain intelligible. This is an independent spatial interpretation of the old design from descriptive text, not a traced or replicated modern museum photograph or museum object.
Composition: camera optic axis vertical, apex exactly centred horizontally and vertically. The main circular/parabolic canopy occupies the centre, four supporting arches and a little peripheral upper gallery framing it towards the corners and wider left/right margins. Peripheral balcony-window wooden latticework is plain, old, unlabelled and restrained. Only dome, structural arches and partial upper gallery visible; no view of paintings, chapel doors, figurative art, marquetry panels, sculpture, museum displays or organ.
Style: real architectural-camera appearance and material texture, natural light entering only through real masonry openings and faint peripheral daylight, muted brown and grey limestone with warm aged wood, soft depth and restrained highlights, no lens flare or exaggerated beams. Photo-like, not painting, illustration, graphic star chart, sci-fi ceiling, HDR, CGI or cinematic lighting.
Constraints: no people, text, letters, numbers, signs, logos, watermark or frame. No modern lamps, electrical fittings, LEDs, museum signage or protected art replicas. Original 1890s architectural interpretation only; do not reproduce an existing interior photograph.
